stories.headline: US strikes Iranian bridges as Tehran readies Houthis to close Red Sea; Brent up 12% on week

key_facts.fact: The US expanded its airstrike campaign against Iran early Friday July 17 by hitting bridges, part of Trump's threat to strike infrastructure to pressure Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States expanded its airstrike campaign against Iran early Friday by increasingly hitting bridges, part of U.S. President Donald Trump's threats to start striking infrastructure to pressure Tehran to ease its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: A US strike on the Bandar-e Khamir bridge in Hormozgan province killed at least seven people and injured nine, according to Iran's Fars news agency, on the sixth consecutive night of US attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: A US attack on the Bandar-e Khamir bridge in the Hormozgan province killed at least seven people and injured nine, according to Iran's Fars news agency.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said the latest wave began at 18:00 GMT Thursday, describing it as an effort to 'further degrade Iranian military capabilities'. Iranian officials say July strikes have killed more than 35 people and wounded over 300.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command said the latest assaults began at 18:00 GMT on Thursday, describing the operation as an effort 'to further degrade Iranian military capabilities'.

key_facts.fact: Iran retaliated on Thursday with missile and drone attacks on Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait, its broadest retaliation of the renewed war; Jordan said eight incoming missiles were intercepted at Al Azraq Air Base.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran responded to the attacks with missile and drone strikes targeting six American-linked bases throughout Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait... Jordanian officials said that eight incoming missiles were intercepted before they reached their intended targets.

key_facts.fact: The US military fired a Hellfire missile into the smokestack of the Curacao-flagged oil tanker Belma near Kharg Island after it ignored multiple warnings, disabling the vessel.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. military said it opened fire on the Curacao-flagged oil tanker Belma sailing toward Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf. After the ship 'ignored multiple warnings,' a U.S. aircraft disabled the merchant vessel by firing a missile into the ship's smokestack.

key_facts.fact: Iran has asked Yemen's Houthi movement to stand ready to close the Red Sea oil export route if the US strikes Iranian power infrastructure, three sources told Reuters, raising the risk of both main Middle East export routes being disrupted at once.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has asked the Houthis to stand ready to close the Red Sea oil route if the U.S. strikes Iranian power infrastructure, three sources told Reuters... 'With the Strait of Hormuz already closed, this threat raises the serious risk of both of the Middle East's primary oil export routes being disrupted at the same time,' said Alex Hodes, director of energy market strategy at brokerage StoneX.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose about 1.25% Friday to near $85 a barrel and WTI to around $80, with both benchmarks up close to 12% on the week.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude rose about $1, or roughly 1.25%, to trade near $85 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate gained a similar amount, or about 1.3%, to around $80, erasing losses from the previous session. Both benchmarks are now up close to 12% for the week.

key_facts.fact: Seven vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, the day after the US reimposed its naval blockade on Iran, down from 13 the previous day. The strait handled about a fifth of daily global oil and LNG trade before the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Seven vessels passed through the strait on Wednesday, the day after the U.S. reimposed its naval blockade on Iran, down from 13 the previous day.

stories.headline: FDA approves Merck's Lipfendra, the first cholesterol pill in a class dominated by injections

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Merck's LIPFENDRA (enlicitide) 20 mg tablets on Thursday July 16, the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor approved to reduce LDL cholesterol in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
key_facts.excerpt: Merck (NYSE: MRK) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved LIPFENDRA (enlicitide) tablets 20 mg as an adjunct to diet and exercise to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).

key_facts.fact: Approval rests on two Phase 3 CORALreef trials: in CORALreef Lipids (2,904 patients) Lipfendra cut LDL-C by 56% versus placebo at week 24; in CORALreef HeFH (303 patients) it cut LDL-C by 59%.
key_facts.excerpt: In CORALreef Lipids, LIPFENDRA reduced LDL-C by 56% compared to placebo at week 24... In CORALreef HeFH, LIPFENDRA reduced LDL-C by 59% at week 24 compared to placebo.

key_facts.fact: Lipfendra is priced at $315 per month before discounts, roughly half the cost of other PCSK9 products on the market.
key_facts.excerpt: Its cost has been set at $315 per month before discounts, Fierce Pharma reported -- roughly half that of other PCSK9 products on the market.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Lipfendra under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) program, which cuts review times from 6-12 months to 1-2 months.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved Lipfendra under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) program, which slashes review times from 6-12 months to 1–2 months for drugs that align with national health priorities.

key_facts.fact: It is not yet known whether Lipfendra reduces cardiovascular morbidity and mortality; a clinical trial is ongoing to determine this.
key_facts.excerpt: While the trials showed that Lipfendra provided reductions in atherogenic lipoproteins associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), it is not yet known if the treatment can reduce the risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, Merck said.

key_facts.fact: The approval bolsters Merck's effort to diversify beyond its blockbuster cancer treatment Keytruda.
key_facts.excerpt: Merck said on Thursday the U.S. FDA has approved its cholesterol pill, the first of its kind to receive the health regulator's nod, bolstering the drugmaker's efforts to diversify beyond its blockbuster cancer treatment Keytruda.

key_facts.fact: In CORALreef HeFH the most common adverse reactions occurring more often than placebo were diarrhea (7% vs 2%) and dizziness (9% vs 4%); safety in CORALreef Lipids was similar to placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: the most common adverse reactions in adults with HeFH treated with LIPFENDRA that occurred at higher frequencies compared to placebo were diarrhea (LIPFENDRA 7%, placebo 2%) and dizziness (LIPFENDRA 9%, placebo 4%).

stories.headline: Kalshi opens betting on clinical trial results and FDA decisions, drawing bioethics backlash

key_facts.fact: Kalshi announced on Thursday July 16 a partnership with public intelligence company AppliedXL to launch a pilot suite of prediction markets on clinical trial outcomes and FDA regulatory decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Kalshi, the next-generation financial exchange, today announced a partnership with public intelligence company AppliedXL to launch a pilot suite of prediction markets on clinical trial outcomes and FDA regulatory decisions.

key_facts.fact: The pilot launched 13 new contracts, including wagers on whether US regulators will approve medicines from Sanofi and Gilead.
key_facts.excerpt: Kalshi Inc. launched 13 new contracts Wednesday allowing traders to bet on clinical trial outcomes and regulatory decisions in the biotechnology sector... The new offerings include wagers on whether U.S. regulators will approve medicines made by companies such as Sanofi (NASDAQ:SNY) and Gilead Sciences Inc. (NASDAQ:GILD).

key_facts.fact: Example contracts at launch include whether AR1001's POLARIS-AD Phase 3 trial will meet its primary endpoint in early Alzheimer's disease, and whether the FDA will approve Gilead/Arcellx's anito-cel for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
key_facts.excerpt: Example contracts available at launch include: Will AR1001's POLARIS-AD Phase 3 trial meet its primary endpoint in early Alzheimer's disease? Will the FDA approve Gilead/Arcellx's anito-cel for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma?

key_facts.fact: Each contract resolves against a named public document — the registered primary endpoint on ClinicalTrials.gov, the FDA approval letter, or the advisory committee vote record — with criteria defined before trading opens.
key_facts.excerpt: Each contract specifies a named public document as its resolution source: the registered primary endpoint on ClinicalTrials.gov... the FDA approval letter, or the advisory committee vote record. AppliedXL defines the criteria for reading that document before the contract opens for trading, not after results arrive.

key_facts.fact: Safeguards limit the pilot to late-stage trials, list contracts only after a trial finishes enrolling, and require traders in these markets to verify their employment.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform is limiting markets to late-stage clinical trials, arguing that earlier studies with exploratory endpoints have a greater insider trading risk. The company also says it will wait until enrollment in a clinical trial is closed before listing a market... Kalshi will also require traders in these markets to verify their employment.

key_facts.fact: Kalshi argues a listed contract produces a 'continuously updated, public probability that reflects the weight of the evidence, rather than the preferred message of the trial sponsor'.
key_facts.excerpt: A publicly listed contract on a drug trial would produce a 'continuously updated, public probability that reflects the weight of the evidence, rather than the preferred message of the trial sponsor', the company said.

key_facts.fact: AppliedXL serves as independent resolution-analysis partner but Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated designated contract market, remains sole and final adjudicator of every contract.
key_facts.excerpt: Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated designated contract market, will operate the markets and remains the sole and final adjudicator of every contract under its exchange rules. AppliedXL will serve as Kalshi's independent resolution-analysis partner... AppliedXL will not make the final settlement decision.

stories.headline: SpaceX aborts Starship Flight 13 at ignition after four Super Heavy engines fail to start

key_facts.fact: SpaceX experienced a last-second abort during the launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 on July 16; on-screen telemetry showed four engines on the Super Heavy booster did not ignite as planned.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX experienced a last-second abort during the launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 on July 16, 2026. On-screen telemetry data showed four engines on the Super Heavy booster didn't ignite as planned, which SpaceX founder Elon Musk said triggered an abort.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX reached ignition of the Super Heavy booster at Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas at 5:45 p.m. CDT (2245 UTC) before the automatic abort.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX reached ignition of the Super Heavy booster at the Pad 2 at SpaceX's Starbase facilities in southern Texas at 5:45 p.m. CDT (6:45 p.m. EDT / 2245 UTC), but on-screen telemetry data showed four engines that apparently didn't ignite as anticipated.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk wrote on X about 10 minutes after the abort: 'Some of the engines didn't start, triggering an automatic launch abort. Next launch attempt hopefully in a few days.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Some of the engines didn't start, triggering an automatic launch abort,' SpaceX founder Elon Musk wrote on his social media site, X, about 10 minutes after the abort. 'Next launch attempt hopefully in a few days.'

key_facts.fact: Flight 13 was to deploy 20 production Starlink V3 satellites, the first of the upgraded Starlinks to fly to space, on a suborbital trajectory; six carry cameras to inspect Ship's heat-shield tiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Ship will carry on with a suborbital trajectory, and is expected to release 20 Starlink V3 satellites — the first of the upgraded Starlinks to fly to space. Six of those spacecraft are equipped with cameras to inspect Ship's heat-shield tiles during flight.

key_facts.fact: Hours earlier the same day, a SpaceX Falcon 9 launched 21 Space Development Agency satellites from Vandenberg at 4:32 p.m. EDT, restarting the Pentagon's first operational low Earth orbit military data network after a nine-month pause.
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on July 16 launched 21 satellites for the Space Force's Space Development Agency, restarting deployment of the Pentagon's first operational low Earth orbit military data network after a months-long pause. The mission, designated T1TL-E, lifted off at 4:32 p.m. Eastern from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

key_facts.fact: With the T1TL-E mission, SDA will have 63 Tranche 1 Transport Layer satellites on orbit, half of the planned 126-satellite Transport Layer.
key_facts.excerpt: SDA's previous Tranche 1 launches placed 21 York satellites in orbit in September 2025 and 21 Lockheed Martin satellites in October 2025. With the latest mission, SDA will have 63 Tranche 1 Transport Layer satellites on orbit, half of the planned 126-satellite Transport Layer for Tranche 1.

stories.headline: PayPal board sees Stripe-Advent's $53B takeover bid as too low, weighing rival offers

key_facts.fact: PayPal's board sees the $53 billion takeover bid by rival Stripe and private equity firm Advent International as undervaluing the company and facing regulatory and financing hurdles, a person familiar with the matter said on July 16.
key_facts.excerpt: PayPal's board sees a $53 billion takeover bid by rival Stripe and private equity firm Advent International as undervaluing the company and facing regulatory and financing hurdles, a person familiar with the matter said, potentially setting the stage for negotiations over the future of the U.S. payments giant.

key_facts.fact: The board's early view is that while the $60.50 per share offer is a premium to PayPal's recent share price, it does not fully reflect the value management could create if its turnaround strategy succeeds. PayPal rose 2% Thursday to $56.73.
key_facts.excerpt: Its early view is that while the $60.50 per share offer represents a premium to the company's recent share price, it does not fully reflect the potential value the company could create over the coming years if management successfully executes its strategy, the source said. PayPal rose 2% on Thursday to $56.73.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley have provided the bidders a roughly $50 billion financing package and are also advising them; Stripe and Advent are contributing $17 billion in equity.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe and Advent are contributing $17 billion in equity for the offer, one of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Under the offer, submitted earlier this month, Stripe and Advent would jointly own PayPal with each holding an equal stake rather than breaking up the company, though they have considered remedies such as divesting Braintree if antitrust regulators object.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the offer, which was submitted earlier this month, Stripe and Advent would jointly own PayPal, with each holding an equal stake rather than breaking up the company, Reuters previously reported. But they have also considered possible remedies should it run afoul of antitrust regulators, one of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: The board is weighing factors beyond price, including certainty of financing, potential regulatory hurdles and a possibly lengthy timeline, and is scheduled to hold additional meetings. It is also evaluating whether other offers could emerge.
key_facts.excerpt: The board is also weighing factors beyond price, including the certainty of financing, potential regulatory hurdles and what could be a lengthy timeline to complete any transaction, the source added. It is scheduled to hold additional meetings, the source said.

key_facts.fact: Stripe enlisted Advent as an equity partner because funding the entire equity portion alone would be difficult; Advent has previously invested in Worldpay, Vantiv and Nuvei.
key_facts.excerpt: Privately held Stripe enlisted Advent as an equity partner because funding the entire equity portion of a deal on its own would be difficult, according to the person familiar with the bid... Advent has been an active investor in the payments sector, with a track record of acquiring and investing in companies across the industry, including Worldpay, Vantiv and, more recently, Nuvei.

stories.headline: China launches Shanghai-based World AI Cooperation Organization with 29 founding countries

key_facts.fact: Twenty-nine countries signed an agreement in Shanghai on Thursday July 16 establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), an independent intergovernmental organization headquartered in Shanghai.
key_facts.excerpt: Twenty-nine countries on Thursday signed an agreement in Shanghai, China, to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO)... Under the agreement, WAICO will be an independent intergovernmental international organization headquartered in Shanghai.

key_facts.fact: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi signed on behalf of China; representatives from 29 countries including Kazakhstan, Laos, Pakistan, Russia and Indonesia became founding members. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres attended the signing ceremony.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and representatives from the 29 countries, including Kazakhstan, Laos, Pakistan, Russia and Indonesia, signed the agreement, state-run Xinhua News Agency reported. The signatories became WAICO's founding members... UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also attended the signing ceremony.

key_facts.fact: At the World AI Conference opening on Friday July 17, Xi Jinping said: 'AI development should not be a solo performance by a single country, but a symphony of international cooperation.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'AI development should not be a solo performance by a single country, but a symphony of international cooperation,' Xi said at the opening of the World Artificial Intelligence Conference.

key_facts.fact: Xi said countries should 'jointly oppose overstretching the national security concept in the field of AI or placing one country's security over that of others', and called for laws, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems to ensure AI stays under human control.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We should jointly oppose overstretching the national security concept in the field of AI or placing one country's security over that of others,' Xi added. 'We should put in place laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning, and emergency response systems, in order to... ensure AI is always under human control.'

key_facts.fact: Xi said China will expand AI cooperation with ASEAN, the League of Arab States, the African Union, CELAC, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS, and promised 30 countries access to a Chinese-developed AI meteorological early-warning system.
key_facts.excerpt: China will expand AI cooperation with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the League of Arab States, the African Union, the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the BRICS countries, Xi said. He promised to provide access for 30 countries to a Chinese-developed AI meteorological system that provides early warning systems.

key_facts.fact: WAICO was first proposed by China in July last year and aims to advance international cooperation and global governance on AI while upholding the purposes of the UN Charter.
key_facts.excerpt: The organisation will 'uphold the purposes of the UN Charter, be committed to extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit and adhere to a people-centred approach,' according to the agreement... WAICO was first proposed by China in July last year.

key_facts.fact: Attendees at the conference included the leaders of Kazakhstan, Cambodia and Thailand and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. American-led restrictions have blocked China from accessing some of the world's most advanced technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: Others attending included the leaders of Kazakhstan, Cambodia and Thailand and U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres... American-led restrictions have blocked China from accessing some of the world's most advanced technologies, spurring China's efforts to build its own know-how.

stories.headline: Dallas Fed's Logan calls for higher rates even as June wholesale inflation falls 0.3%

key_facts.fact: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on July 16 that she currently believes 'modestly higher interest rates would better balance' the FOMC's goals, arguing inflation 'has been too high, for too long, and does not appear to be on track all the way back to 2 percent'.
key_facts.excerpt: To sum up, inflation has been too high, for too long, and does not appear to be on track all the way back to 2 percent. And the inflation risks are to the [upside]... So, I currently believe modestly higher interest rates would better balance the FOMC's [goals].

key_facts.fact: Logan said the unemployment rate averaged 4.3% in the first half of 2026 and employers added an average of 92,000 jobs per month, describing the labor market as 'well balanced and perhaps even strengthening a bit'.
key_facts.excerpt: The unemployment rate averaged 4.3 percent in the first half of this year. That is about the same as a year earlier and near most estimates of the lowest sustainable level. Employers added an average of 92,000 jobs per month in the first half of this year, modestly outpacing growth in the size of the labor force. Overall, the labor market is well balanced and perhaps even strengthening a bit.

key_facts.fact: US wholesale inflation fell 0.3% from May to June on plunging energy prices, a softer reading than the unchanged result economists polled by Dow Jones expected, but intensifying hostilities with Iran are clouding the outlook.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. wholesale inflation fell from May to June on plunging energy prices, but intensifying hostilities with Iran are clouding the outlook.

key_facts.fact: Jobless claims for the week ending July 11 fell 8,000 to 208,000, below the 217,000-218,000 expected and the lowest since early May; continuing claims fell to 1.805 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Both the initial and continuing segments fell during the past two weeks to 208k and 1.805 million from 216k and 1.821 million for the seven-day periods ending on July 11 and July 4. Additionally, the indicators were beneath the median estimates of 217k and 1.820 million.

key_facts.fact: Retail sales rose 0.2% in June, down sharply from May's revised 1% increase and below the 0.3% expected; excluding gas stations, spending rose 0.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: Retail sales rose 0.2% in June from the prior month, the Commerce Department said Thursday, down sharply from May's revised 1% increase. That was lower than expectations of a 0.3% increase... Excluding sales at gas stations, spending in June [was] up by a solid 0.7%.

key_facts.fact: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said inflation remains 1.7 percentage points above the 2% target and that inflation risks now outweigh employment risks, citing two unexpected price shocks this year: the Middle East conflict and higher capital spending on AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Cook highlighted that inflation remains 1.7 percentage points above the target, despite softer recent reports... Adding, the US economy has been hit by two unexpected price shocks this year--the Middle East conflict and higher capital spending on AI infrastructure--she said inflation risks now outweigh employment risks compared with a year ago.

key_facts.fact: After the softer PPI print, the CME FedWatch tool showed the projected chance of a September rate hike falling to 17% from 47% the previous morning.
key_facts.excerpt: The CME Fedwatch is now projecting only a 17% chance of a September hike vs. the 47% chance yesterday morning... Core PPI rose 4.7%, below the 5.1% expectation.
